answer.headline: Brew excellent pour-over coffee by using a 1:16 coffee-to-water ratio, filtered water at 93°C, and a steady, circular pouring technique.
body: Pour-over coffee is a method that highlights the nuanced flavors of specialty beans by allowing precise control over extraction variables. The process relies on gravity to slowly pass hot water through a bed of ground coffee in a filter, ensuring a clean cup with high clarity.

The keys to success are consistency in your grind size, temperature control, and agitation management. By pouring in stages—a small initial bloom followed by controlled pulses of water—you release trapped CO2 and ensure an even extraction that avoids bitterness while preventing under-extracted sourness.
caveats: Results vary based on your specific dripper geometry.
Coffee roast profile may require slight adjustments to grind size.
Water quality significantly impacts final flavor profile.

facts: Use a burr grinder for consistent particles.

modules.headline: Step-by-step brewing guide

items.label: Pre-rinse
items.detail: Place the filter in the dripper and rinse it with hot water to remove any paper taste and warm your vessel.

items.label: Grind coffee
items.detail: Grind your beans to a consistency resembling sea salt; use 20g of coffee for 320g of water.

items.label: Bloom
items.detail: Pour 40g of water (double the dry weight) over the grounds and wait for the gas to escape.

items.label: Pour
items.detail: Pour the remaining water in slow, circular motions, avoiding the very edges of the filter to prevent bypassing.

items.label: Draw down
items.detail: Allow the water to pass through the bed; the total time from first pour should be around 3:00 to 3:30.

facts: Grind size determines draw down time.
modules.headline: Guidelines for consistent extraction

items.label: Coffee tastes sour
items.detail: The grind is likely too coarse or water too cool; adjust finer or hotter.

items.label: Coffee tastes bitter
items.detail: The grind is too fine or the contact time is too long; adjust coarser.

items.label: Clogged filter
items.detail: Often caused by poor grinder quality creating too many 'fines' (dust).
